rationale: PINS THE REFUSAL, NOT AN EMISSION: `using L for T` must publish `references` to the library and must NEVER publish `mixes_in`, INCLUDING for the two declared-host forms a declared-host rule would have published (`using MathLib for Price`, `using MathLib for Amount`). THE REASON IS THE VOCABULARY'S OWN DEFINITION, not the absence of a source symbol: `mixes_in` (src/ast/types.ts) is a class composing a mixin INTO ITS SUPERTYPE CHAIN, and the mixin is a supertype MEMBER. PHP trait `use` flattens members into the class's method table and Go embedding promotes them into the struct's method set; Solidity adds NO member to the type — `Price` is still `uint128`, its ABI and chain are untouched, and `p.double()` binds as `MathLib.double(p)` only where the directive is in scope (`global` widens the SCOPE, not the type). The composing actor is the scope, not the type, so a `mixes_in` row would name the wrong actor as well as the wrong relation — and it would land in a bucket two consumers read as supertype composition (src/intelligence/graph/graph-engine.ts, src/intelligence/analysis/complexity.ts). THE DEPENDENCY IS NOT LOST: the `references` row for the same directive is asserted here, and it is the true relation (the file READ the name). THE CONSTRUCT POPULATION IS MEASURED: 124 `using_directive` sites in 76 files, 27 with a declared host and one library, 0 of which add a member to the type (validation/m14/measurements/solidity-extended-census.json). THE OTHER TWO RULED TYPES ARE PINNED BESIDE IT: `renders` (markup TEXT from a pure function is a value, and the vocabulary has 0 component symbol kinds) and `part_of` (a Solidity import is a MODULE load — each source unit is compiled in its own scope and the import brings symbols INTO it — while a part shares one scope and imports nothing). `new Market()` is the positive control a render rule must not steal: it is `instantiates`.

expectRelationships.comment: THE TRUE RELATION, pinned as the positive half: the directive READS the library's name, and that row survives the refusal — so nothing is lost by not publishing `mixes_in`. The source is the enclosing contract, because that is the scope the directive is written in.
the CONFORMANCE construct, pinned beside the refused composition: a class header is extends/implements, so 'no conformance declared' can never be used to relabel it
SOL-5's discriminator: an in-file interface ancestor is implements

the part_of negative read the RIGHT way — a module load is imports

expectRelationshipCount.comment: THE REFUSAL, AS A COUNT. Five `using_directive` nodes exist in this file — two with a DECLARED host (Price, Amount), one primitive host, one braced set, one wildcard — and NONE may publish `mixes_in`. A rule keyed on the node type would publish 5; a rule that only required a declared host would publish 2; both are wrong for the same reason, which is why the two declared-host forms are forbidden explicitly rather than left to the count.
the RULING, pinned as a count: Solidity's import is a module load (its own scope, symbols brought in), not a part sharing one scope
the third ruling, pinned as a count, in a file that contains a markup-producing function AND a construction

forbidRelationships.comment: FORBID (1) — THE FORM A DECLARED-HOST RULE PUBLISHED. `Price` is a declared user-defined value type and `MathLib` is a declared library, and the row is still false: no member of MathLib enters Price's declared surface. This is the one that must go red if the emission is ever restored.
FORBID (2) — the struct host: same refusal, and the host test reading the TYPE namespace rather than the inheritance namespace is what made this form reachable in the first place
FORBID (3) — a primitive host has no source symbol at all: a second, independent reason the row is impossible
FORBID (4) — the wildcard form names no host type
FORBID (5) — the braced form's composed set is a LIST OF FUNCTIONS; naming the function as the mixin would assert a member set that is not one declaration

the wrong-source edge the enclosing contract invites: a rule reading 'the contract carrying the using' as the source would emit Market -> MathLib four times. Refused for the same reason the host-sourced reading is: the composing actor is neither the contract nor the host, it is the SCOPE.

FORBID — no part_of at all: a Solidity import creates its own module scope and imports symbols, which is the opposite of a shared single scope
